To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Wfs1 is required in layer 2/ 3 pyramidal neurons to moderate stress-induced depressive behaviors.

Wfs1 is expressed in layer 2/ 3 pyramidal neurons and deletion of Wfs 1 from these cells results in increased stress induced depressive behaviors, and altered accumulation of growth and neurotrophin factors.
Wfs1 is required in mPFC L2/3 PCs for stress resilience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes stress and how this processing is altered in depression and anxiety.
the molecular and cellular basis of depression and how it can be treated.
the role of the medial prefront frontal cortex (mPFP), a part of the brain involved in depression, in moderating stress induced depressive behaviors and the underlying mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Wfs1 is a critical gene in pyramidal neurons of layer 2/ 3 of the medial prefrontol cortex (mPfc).

the Wfs1 gene plays an important role in the regulation of the stress axis, and that its absence leads to a dysregulation of the hypothalalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis, which is the cause of the depressive-like phenotype in mice with Wfs1 deficiency.
WFS1 is involved in the regulation of the HPA axis, the neurotrophin system, and the neuroendocrine system, and that these are important for the development of depression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a specific cell type in the medial pre-frontal cortex that is necessary for the ability of the medial pre-frontcortex to regulate stress responses.
the mPFC is a critical structure in regulating stress-induced depressive behaviors.
the loss of WFS1 in pyramidal neurons of the superficial layer 2-3 in the mPFOC leads to the development of depressive behaviors in response stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the superficial layer of the medial prefronta l cortex (mP FC) is critical for the ability to suppress stress induced depressive behaviors and that Wfs1 is required for the proper function of these cells.
the superficial layer 2 and layer 3 pyramidal neurons of the medial prefront cortex (mPfc) play a critical role in moderating depressive behaviors in response acute and chronic stress.
the superficial layers of the mPfc are important for the moderation of stress-induced depressive-like behaviors, and that this effect is dependent upon the presence of Wfs1 in these cells.
